arxiv-2005-13797.title: 3D human pose estimation with adaptive receptive fields and dilated temporal convolutions
arxiv-2005-13797.creator: Eduardo Castillo, Irene Font Peradejordi, Michael Shin, Shobhna Jayaraman
arxiv-2005-13797.description: Abstract In this work, we demonstrate that receptive fields in 3D pose estimation can be effectively specified using optical flow. We introduce adaptive receptive fields, a simple and effective method to aid receptive field selection in pose estimation models based on optical flow inference.

arxiv-2108-06795.title: Fragments in symmetric configurations with block size 3
arxiv-2108-06795.creator: Grahame Erskine, Terry Griggs, Jozef Širáň
arxiv-2108-06795.description: Abstract We begin the study of collections of three blocks which can occur in a symmetric configuration with block size 3, v 3 v_{3} . Formulae are derived for the number of occurrences of these and it is shown that the triangle, i.e. abf, ace, bcd is a basis.

arxiv-2112-15255.title: Antimatter in the Milky Way
arxiv-2112-15255.creator: A. D. Dolgov
arxiv-2112-15255.description: Abstract Recent astronomical observations indicating a strikingly abundant presence of antimatter in the Galaxy, in particular, of anti-stars are reviewed. Long-time earlier theoretical predictions are briefly discussed. a Department of Physics, Novosibirsk State University, Pirogova st. 2, Novosibirsk, 630090 Russia b Bogolyubov Laboratory of Theoretical Physics, Joint Institute for Nuclear Research, Joliot-Curie st.

arxiv-2307-09922.title: Information Structures in AC/DC Grids
arxiv-2307-09922.creator: Josh A. Taylor
arxiv-2307-09922.description: Abstract The converters in an AC/DC grid form actuated boundaries between the AC and DC subgrids. We show how in both simple linear and balanced dq -frame models, the states on either side of these boundaries are coupled only by control inputs. This topological property imparts all AC/DC grids with poset-causal information structures.

arxiv-2312-17196.title: The emergence of Einstein gravity from topological supergravity in 3 + 1 3+1 D
arxiv-2312-17196.creator: Tianyao Fang, Zheng-Cheng Gu
arxiv-2312-17196.description: Abstract The topological aspects of Einstein gravity suggest that topological invariance could be a more profound principle in understanding quantum gravity. In this work, we explore a topological supergravity action that initially describes a universe without Riemann curvature, which seems trivial.

arxiv-2405-19597.title: SVFT : Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning with Singular Vectors
arxiv-2405-19597.creator: Vijay Lingam, Atula Tejaswi, Aditya Vavre, Aneesh Shetty, Gautham Krishna Gudur, Joydeep Ghosh, Alex Dimakis, Eunsol Choi, Aleksandar Bojchevski, Sujay Sanghavi
arxiv-2405-19597.description: Abstract Popular parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods, such as LoRA and its variants, freeze pre-trained model weights 𝐖 \mathbf{W} and inject learnable matrices 𝚫 ​ 𝐖 \mathbf{\Delta W} . These 𝚫 ​ 𝐖 \mathbf{\Delta W} matrices are structured for efficient parameterization, often using techniques like low-rank approximations or scaling vectors.

arxiv-2410-21963.title: NLO EW corrections to tau pair production via photon fusion in Pb-Pb ultraperipheral collision
arxiv-2410-21963.creator: Jun Jiang, Peng-Cheng Lu, Zong-Guo Si, Han Zhang, Xin-Yi Zhang
arxiv-2410-21963.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jun Jiang, Peng-Cheng Lu, Zong-Guo Si, Han Zhang, Xin-Yi Zhang. We study the next-to-leading order (NLO) electroweak (EW) corrections to the γ ​ γ → τ + ​ τ − \gamma\gamma\to\tau^{+}\tau^{-} process in Pb-Pb ultraperipheral collision (UPC). We find that the EW correction δ ​ σ EW \delta\sigma_{\mathrm{EW}} decreases the total cross section σ NLO = σ LO + δ ​ σ EW \sigma_{\mathrm{NLO}}=\sigma_{\mathrm{LO}}+\delta\sigma_{\mathrm{EW}} by -3% at Pb-Pb center-of-mass energy s N ​ N = 5.02 \sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02 TeV.

arxiv-2504-21198.title: Graph Synthetic Out-of-Distribution Exposure with Large Language Models
arxiv-2504-21198.creator: Haoyan Xu, Zhengtao Yao, Ziyi Wang, Zhan Cheng, Xiyang Hu, Mengyuan Li, Yue Zhao
arxiv-2504-21198.description: Abstract Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection in graphs is critical for ensuring model robustness in open-world and safety-sensitive applications. Existing graph OOD detection approaches typically train an in-distribution (ID) classifier on ID data alone, then apply post-hoc scoring to detect OOD instances.

arxiv-2505-09683.title: Euler topology in classical spin liquids
arxiv-2505-09683.creator: Luca Rüegg, Arthur Morris, Han Yan (闫寒), Robert-Jan Slager
arxiv-2505-09683.description: Abstract Classical spin liquids have recently been analyzed in view of the single-gap homotopy classification of their dispersive eigenvectors. We show that the recent progress in defining multi-gap topologies, notably exemplified by the Euler class, can be naturally included in these homotopy-based classification schemes and present phases that change topology by band node braiding.

arxiv-2511-19410.title: Powers of abelian varieties over ℚ ⁡ ( t ) ¯ \overline{\mathbb{Q}(t)} not isogenous to a Jacobian
arxiv-2511-19410.creator: Olivier de Gaay Fortman and Ananth N. Shankar
arxiv-2511-19410.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Olivier de Gaay Fortman and Ananth N. Shankar. We prove the existence of abelian varieties over ℚ ⁡ ( t ) ¯ \overline{\mathbb{Q}(t)} with no power isogenous to a Jacobian. Moreover, given a positive integer N N , we prove the existence of abelian varieties over ℚ ⁡ ( t ) ¯ \overline{\mathbb{Q}(t)} with maximal monodromy such that the n n th power is not isogenous to a Jacobian for n ≤ N n\leq N .

arxiv-2512-19839.title: Using the Landau gauge gluon propagator to set the lattice physical scales and understanding the finite size effects
arxiv-2512-19839.creator: Orlando Oliveira, Paulo J Silva
arxiv-2512-19839.description: Abstract A crucial step in extracting physical predictions from lattice QCD simulations is the scale setting, i.e. the determination of the lattice spacing ( a a ) in physical units. Herein, the relative scale setting for different β \beta ’s is discussed, using the Landau gauge gluon propagator computed with large statistical ensembles.

pmc-11665400.title: Dipeptidyl peptidase 4 as an injury-responsive protein in the mouse sciatic nerve
pmc-11665400.creator: Yeonsoo Oh, Yongcheol Cho
pmc-11665400.description: Dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP4) is a membrane-bound protease known for its roles in immunity and metabolism; however, its function in the nervous system remains largely unexplored. We found that DPP4 is predominantly expressed in the Schwann cells of the sciatic nerve, and its systemic depletion in postnatal mice resulted in a decline in motor function.

pmc-11675540.title: Effects of Combination Taping Technique on Disability, Functional Capacity, and Knee Isokinetic Torque in Patients with Knee Osteoarthritis: A Blinded Randomized Controlled Study
pmc-11675540.creator: Nouf H. Alkhamees, Osama R. Abdelraouf, Olfat Ibrahim Ali, Zizi M. Ibrahim, Amal A. Elborady
pmc-11675540.description: Background: Treatments that combine both elastic and rigid taping in knee osteoarthritis have not yet been investigated in the literature. Thus, the purpose of the present study is to investigate how the combination taping technique affects functional status, disability, and quadricep isokinetic torque in cases of knee osteoarthritis.

pmc-12468349.title: Real-World Adoption of Adjuvant Therapies for Resected Stage IB–III Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer
pmc-12468349.creator: Arvind Kumar, Steven Tohmasi, Daniel B Eaton, Nahom Seyoum, Whitney S Brandt, Theodore S Thomas, Martin W Schoen, Nikki E Rossetti, Su-Hsin Chang, Yan Yan, Mayank R Patel, Sara Malone, Molly C Tokaz, Bryan F Meyers, Benjamin D Kozower, Varun Puri, Brendan T Heiden, Myung-Ju Ahn
pmc-12468349.description: Simple SummaryAlthough standard-of-care treatment for high-risk early-stage or locally advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) includes adjuvant chemotherapy following surgical resection, various barriers have been reported that prevent patients from receiving recommended adjuvant treatment. Further addition of adjuvant immunotherapy and molecularly targeted agents has improved short- and long-term outcomes for patients with NSCLC.

pmc-12713232.title: High BRAF variant allele frequency predicts poor outcomes in metastatic melanoma patients treated with BRAF/MEK inhibitors
pmc-12713232.creator: Michele Guida, Benedetta Apollonio, Luca Romano, Francesco Spagnolo, Pietro Quaglino, Roberta Depenni, Rosamaria Pinto, Teresa Squicciarini, Livia Fucci, Piergiorgio Di Tullio, Maria Chiara Scaini, Maria Teresa Maccallini, Alice Indini, Teresa Troiani, Iole Natalicchio, Sonia Brugnara, Maurizio Lomb
pmc-12713232.description: BackgroundBRAF/MEK inhibitors have improved the outcome in metastatic melanoma (MM) patients harboring a BRAF mutation, but no biomarker predictive of response has been identified.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective analysis on 264 MM patients that had received first-line targeted therapy with BRAF/MEK inhibitors.

pmc-12992493.title: Critical care utilization associated with an electronic dance music festival in Las Vegas, Nevada: A retrospective cohort study of the electric daisy carnival
pmc-12992493.creator: Jie Ren, Kavita Batra, Vidhani Goel, Taya Jensen, San Tran, Mutsumi Kioka
pmc-12992493.description: IntroductionElectronic dance music (EDM) festivals are associated with recreational drug use and medical emergencies, yet comparative data on the severity of festival-related overdoses are limited. This study compared hospital outcomes, particularly critical care utilization, between patients transported from the Electric Daisy Carnival (EDC) and those with non–festival-related overdoses during the same period.

pmc-13021659.title: Prognostic value of serial alactic base excess measurements in patients with sepsis: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13021659.creator: Dursun Elmas, Muhammet Cemal Kizilarslanoglu
pmc-13021659.description: BackgroundThis study evaluated the prognostic significance of serial alactic base excess (ABE) measurements in patients with sepsis.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective cohort study including 521 adult patients with sepsis. Arterial blood gas analyses obtained at 0, 6, 12, 24, and 48 h were used to calculate ABE.

pmc-13154674.title: Quality management of comprehensive blood conservation strategies during cardiopulmonary bypass in pediatric cardiac surgery
pmc-13154674.creator: Wenting Wang, He Wang, Jia Liu, Yu Jin, Jinping Liu
pmc-13154674.description: BackgroundPediatric cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) carries substantial transfusion requirements, exposing patients to increased risks of complications during hospital stay. This study evaluates the clinical impact of a quality-controlled, multimodal blood conservation strategy during CPB in pediatric cardiac surgery.

pmc-13330920.title: Harmonization and integration of pharmacogenomics screens
pmc-13330920.creator: Aleysha T Chen, Marcus R Kelly, Trey Ideker, Nicole M Mattson, Christina Kendziorski
pmc-13330920.description: MotivationLarge pharmacogenomics screens have generated a wealth of information cataloguing the responses of more than a thousand tumor cell-line models to FDA-approved and exploratory drugs. Although centralized repositories have consolidated data access, the diversity of experimental platforms and response metrics used in these screens have made it challenging to integrate and compare their measured drug responses.

pmc-13429668.title: Caenorhabditis elegans in neuroscience: from neural communication to neurodegenerative disease modeling
pmc-13429668.creator: Ziheng Pan, Yunlong Shen, Dejian Peng, Li Tang, Tianlu Ran, Yaohui Liu, Xinyi Zeng, Hui Liu
pmc-13429668.description: Consistent with humans and other metazoans, the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans) undergoes progressive structural and functional decline during aging. Possessing highly conserved genetic pathways that share extensive homology with human genes, and characterized by a streamlined, fully mapped connectome, C. elegans has emerged as a robust model for dissecting the mechanisms underlying neuronal aging and degeneration.
